title: Wife’s death spurs Maharashtra man to build village road
content: Villagers in Ghodankappi are building their own road after a woman's death highlighted connectivity issues. Tulsiram Gedam mobilized residents to construct the vital 1.5-km stretch. This initiative underscores the administration's failure to provide basic infrastructure to remote settlements. The villagers seek safe access for children, elderly, and patients. Administration has now initiated steps to improve the village's road connectivity.

title: Rs 16-for-16-minute offer sparks chaos at Kanpur market, FIR lodged
content: The unveiling of a Rs 16 garment promo ignited pandemonium in Kanpur's Alam Market, with throngs of people converging and causing significant traffic snarls and a near-stampede scenario. Law enforcement quickly acted to clear the scene once the store closed. The turmoil left several shoppers injured, prompting police to file an FIR against the shop owner and other responsible individuals.

title: 'Godfather of AI' agrees with Elon Musk: Mass unemployment is coming and worse
content: Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel laureate known as the "Godfather of AI", says Elon Musk  is right that AI will end most jobs. Speaking with Senator Bernie Sanders at Georgetown University, the AI pioneer warned of massive unemployment, arguing Big Tech's trillion-dollar data centre spending only pays off by replacing workers cheaply. Sanders estimates nearly 100 million US jobs face automation risk.

title: UP horror: Man assaults delivery agent over ‘small’ delay, arrested
content: A delivery executive faced assault from a customer in Meerut over a slight order delay. The customer, a bank manager, allegedly threatened the worker with false accusations. CCTV footage captured the altercation before the worker was taken inside the flat. The victim reported threats of death and attempts to steal his money. Police arrested the accused manager and registered a case against him.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40bn in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott's philanthropic efforts have made a significant impact by enabling the cancellation of medical debt across the United States. By purchasing and eliminating patient debt at a minimal cost, she has set a precedent that encourages other wealthy individuals to invest in similar initiatives. Despite these immediate acts of generosity, the need for comprehensive policy reforms persists, as true transformation necessitates addressing the fundamental issues leading to medical debt.

title: Nebraska bridge heats itself from inside to melt snow during storms
content: A Nebraska bridge is using 52 slabs of conductive concrete that can heat its surface and melt snow and ice during winter storms. Developed by University of Nebraska-Lincoln professor Chris Tuan, the technology uses steel shavings and carbon particles to carry electricity through the concrete. The system could reduce the need for de-icing chemicals at bridges, airport tarmacs, intersections and other icy areas.

title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes a 'vacation request' to employees for this month
content: Accenture's CEO, Julie Sweet, has requested that employees delay their vacation in August. This temporary policy adjustment is designed to bolster staff presence as the company approaches the end of its financial year. Following disappointing quarterly results and a forecasted drop in revenue, Accenture is permitting employees to carry over unused vacation days into the next fiscal year to help enhance fourth-quarter outputs and revenue generation.

title: Suriya's 'Vishwanath and Sons' sees decent Monday run
content: Suriya's latest project, 'Vishwanth and Sons', has made waves at the box office by surpassing the impressive Rs 100 crore milestone in its opening weekend. The film continues to perform well through its initial weekdays, with the Tamil version garnering Rs 67 lakh and the Telugu version adding Rs 50 lakh. Overall, the film's net collection in India has climbed to around Rs 59.32 crore.

title: Odisha removes six-attempt cap for OCS exam, general candidates can now appear till age 42
content: Odisha has removed the six-attempt ceiling for candidates appearing for the Odisha Civil Services examination. Under the revised rules, eligible unreserved-category aspirants can now take the exam repeatedly until they reach the upper age limit of 42 years. The state has also expanded free textbooks to Classes IX and X and announced plans to strengthen school education.

title: JD(S) leader arrested for assaulting Bengaluru traffic constable on duty - video
content: JD(S) leader Manjunath was arrested for allegedly assaulting a traffic constable on duty. The incident occurred when the constable stopped Manjath's vehicle to regulate traffic flow. An argument escalated, and Manjath reportedly grabbed the constable by his collar. A viral video shows Manjath speaking to a senior officer and attempting to kick the constable. Police registered a case and subsequently arrested Manjath for obstructing a public servant.

title: Maera Mishra Announces Pregnancy: TV actress and Rajul Yadav expecting first child
content: Actress Maera Mishra and her husband Rajul Yadav are thrilled to share the news of their first pregnancy. In a touching video posted on social media, Maera proudly showcased her growing baby bump. Warm wishes and congratulations poured in from friends and colleagues in the television industry, marking this joyful milestone as a new and exciting chapter for the couple following their wedding.

title: Matrimonial site promised 100 matches, delivered 51; Kerala panel orders Rs 15K refund
content: A matrimonial website was found deficient in service by the Kerala consumer commission. The website promised one hundred contacts but only provided fifty-one during the subscription. The commission reduced the refund amount from the district commission's order. It noted that fifty-one contacts were indeed provided to the complainant. The company's appeal was dismissed while confirming the deficiency finding.

title: Trump admin crackdown: Indian techies see biggest hit as US green card approvals plunge sharply
content: The approval rate for EB-1A, the US green card category meant for individuals with extraordinary ability, has dropped sharply in FY26, with Indian applicants bearing a significant share of the impact, according to several immigration experts.

title: Rohan Naidu: From engineering dropout to probing the early universe
content: Rohan Naidu, an astronomer from Hyderabad, is making significant contributions to our understanding of the early universe. His recent study focuses on a cosmic dawn object that reveals a supermassive black hole enveloped by dense gas. This important research not only sheds light on the rapid growth of early black holes but may also provide insights into the enigmatic 'little red dots' recently detected by the Webb telescope.

title: Awarapan 2 box office collection day 4: Emraan film nears Rs 85 crore
content: Emraan Hashmi's 'Awarapan 2' has emerged as the standout performer of the Independence Day box office clash, and the sequel to the 2007 cult favourite is now closing in on a major milestone. After a stellar extended weekend, the film enters its first working Monday, typically a day of correction, but with a total that already has trade watchers talking about the Rs. 100 crore mark. Here's a live look at how Day 4 is shaping up.

title: How India’s WTC final hopes hurt after Bangladesh's win over Australia: Explained

title: 'Minor portion' of Ganga Expressway sinks amid heavy rain
content: A section of the Ganga Expressway near Bijnor sank due to heavy rainfall.  The road developed a depression and pothole-like damage on August 14.  Authorities dispatched a maintenance team which promptly began repair work.  The affected road surface was restored soon after the damage was detected.  Traffic on the expressway is currently running normally after the swift repairs.

title: 2 more Air India pilots fail to clear dope test after Phuket-Delhi flight scare
content: Air India's recent pilot screening revealed two non-negative dope test results, leading to these pilots being grounded while awaiting confirmatory tests. In response, the aviation ministry has instructed the DGCA to revise current dope testing protocols. The intended policy overhaul aims to impose stricter penalties for pilots found using illegal drugs, while also distinguishing between accidental use of medication and intentional substance abuse.

title: 'We owe them our solidarity': Rahul writes to ally Soren over student protests
content: Rahul Gandhi has thrown his weight behind students protesting against the irregularities in Jharkhand's recruitment exams. He has called on Chief Minister Hemant Soren to engage with student representatives amid an ongoing indefinite hunger strike by some. Gandhi emphasized that the Congress party stands in complete solidarity with the students, voicing concerns over the exploitation of the Indian education system by certain factions.

title: Hours after CJP's school inspection call, Rajasthan bars outsiders from campuses
content: Rajasthan's education department has restricted outsider entry into schools without principal permission. This directive follows the Cockroach Janta Party's announcement of a statewide campaign. The CJP plans to inspect dilapidated government schools across nine districts over two weeks. Volunteers will raise student issues as the administration has ignored repair demands. The group warns of a movement if a plan for classroom repairs is not presented.

title: Apple told to pay Rs 45,500 to customer after iPhone overheats, faces network issues
content: A Haryana consumer commission ordered Apple India to refund Rs 45,500 for a defective iPhone 15.  The customer complained about repeated overheating and connectivity issues with the device.  Apple claimed unauthorized modifications, but the commission found no proof of tampering.  The company also must pay Rs 10,000 for compensation and costs.  The ruling highlights Apple's liability for service deficiencies during warranty.

title: 300 guards jump in unison to test Mahakaleshwar temple bridge before Nag Panchami
content: Over 300 security guards performed a load test on a new foot overbridge.  Engineers inspected the bridge for structural integrity and signs of corrosion.  The 91-foot-long bridge will carry thousands of devotees to the Nagchandreshwar temple.  Authorities recommend a maximum of 300 devotees use the bridge simultaneously.  The bridge was constructed in 2022 and passed its recent safety inspection.

title: Gold price prediction today: Will gold prices continue to rally?

title: A threat hiding in plane sight: Why the food on our plates may be riskier than we think
content: food adulteration rarely arrives with the drama of a terrorist attack . it is quieter and more insidious an assault, on something we consume routinely and trust almost instinctively . we have built elaborate systems to protect the nation from exceptional threats .

title: Iran nuclear post: How a fabricated X claim by Indian account created panic in Israel, US
content: the false claim emerged on august 5 when an anonymous account on X in India posted that Brig. Gen. Ahmad Vahidi had said Iran would not abandon its nuclear weapons ambitions as long as Israel and the United States possessed such weapons . the claim quickly gained traction, with Israeli accounts and media outlets repeating it before it reached senior political figures in the united states .

title: Disproportionate assets case: SC asks Allahabad HC not to proceed against Rahul
content: the apex court asked the Allahabad high court not to proceed with case against Rahul Gandhi . the top court also directed the CBI and Enforcement Directorate not to submit any probe report to any authority . if the complainant’s allegations were found to be true, the matter would amount to a “gross disproportionate assets case”

title: How Trump bypassed Iran's negotiators and used Kurdistan's Barzani to contact IRGC
content: the move allowed Washington to bypass Iran’s official negotiators, including parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, amid growing doubts over whether they had the authority to speak for the IRGC . the concerns emerged in mid-may, as a u.s. negotiating team began questioning whether Iran was actually in a position to make commitments to the powerful military force .

title: Iran offers $30,000 bounty for killing, capturing US soldiers; $60,000 if done by women
content: the reward doubles to $60,000 if the act is carried out by an Iranian woman . the announcement comes amid ongoing tensions between Tehran and Washington . there is no known deployment of US ground troops inside Iran . amir Hatami says the plan was drawn up following "the large number of requests"
